original_question: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Is f(n) a nondecreasing function of n; that is, does f(n + 1) >= f(n) for all positive integers n?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problems: "As a much simpler task, David S. Newman has mentioned that it would be nice to have a proof that f(n) is nondecreasing," where f(n)=|T(n)| counts Wilf partitions. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct counting function f(n): the number of partitions of n whose nonzero part-multiplicities are all distinct, and it spells out the monotonicity issue in the explicit form f(n+1) ≥ f(n) for all positive integers n. That is exactly the open problem isolated in the paper’s Open Problems section. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))
missing_details: The paper introduces the notation T(n) for the set of such partitions and writes f(n)=|T(n)|; using that notation makes the question closer to the paper’s own formulation. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))

The paper names these partitions Wilf partitions; adding that label makes the question more paper-faithful and recognizable. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))

To be fully stand-alone, it helps to say explicitly that these are ordinary integer partitions into positive parts, and that the multiplicities being compared are the positive multiplicities of the distinct part sizes that actually occur. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))

In the paper this is posed as an open problem/request for a proof of monotonicity, not as a numbered conjecture, so the refined version should be framed as determining whether the sequence is monotone. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))
refined_question: Let T(n) be the set of ordinary integer partitions of the positive integer n in which the multiplicities of the distinct part sizes that occur are pairwise distinct (these are the Wilf partitions), and let f(n)=|T(n)|. Is it true that f(n+1) ≥ f(n) for every integer n ≥ 1?
justification: Sections 1 and 2 set up Wilf’s problem and define T(n) and f(n)=|T(n)| for partitions whose nonzero multiplicities are all different. The paper’s main theorem, Theorem 3.1, concerns the first-order asymptotics of ln f(n). Your draft is not aiming at that theorem itself; rather, it matches the separate open problem stated later in Section 5, where the authors explicitly single out monotonicity of f(n) as a desirable simpler task. So the sharp, paper-faithful refinement is the monotonicity question for the exact sequence f(n)=|T(n)|, with the quantifier stated explicitly as n ≥ 1. ([combinatorics.org](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v19i2p18/pdf/))
